From Wiktionary, the free dictionary
See also: férié and férie

English

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Middle English ferie, from Old French ferie, from Latin feriae (“holidays”). See fair.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈfɪəɹi/
  • Audio (Southern England):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɪəɹi

Noun

[edit]

ferie (plural feries)

  1. (obsolete) A holiday.

References

[edit]
  • “ferie”, in Webster’s Revised Unabridged Dictionary, Springfield, Mass.: G. & C. Merriam, 1913, →OCLC.

Anagrams

[edit]
  • firee, ifere

Danish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Latin fēriae (“festival, rest”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈfeɐ̯ˀiə], [ˈfeɐ̯ˀjə]

Noun

[edit]

ferie c (singular definite ferien, plural indefinite ferier)

  1. holiday
  2. vacation
  3. recess

Declension

[edit]
Declension of ferie
common
gender 		singular plural
indefinite definite indefinite definite
nominative ferie ferien ferier ferierne
genitive feries feriens feriers feriernes

Further reading

[edit]
  • “ferie” in Den Danske Ordbog
  • “ferie” in Ordbog over det danske Sprog
  • ferie on the Danish Wikipedia.Wikipedia da

Italian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • Audio:(file)

Noun

[edit]

ferie f

  1. plural of feria
  2. holidays, vacation

Anagrams

[edit]
  • fiere

Middle English

[edit]

Etymology 1

[edit]

    Partially from Old Norse ferja; partially a back-formation from ferien.

    Alternative forms

    [edit]
    • fery, ferye, ffery, verye

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): /ˈfɛriː(ə)/

    Noun

    [edit]

    ferie (plural feries)

    1. A place where a ferry crosses.
    2. (rare) A ferry.
    Descendants
    [edit]
    • English: ferry (see there for further descendants)
    • Scots: ferry
    References
    [edit]
    • “feri(e, n.(2).”, in MED Online, Ann Arbor, Mich.: University of Michigan, 2007.

    Etymology 2

    [edit]

      From Old French ferie, from Medieval Latin fēria; compare feyre.

      Alternative forms

      [edit]
      • feri, fery, ferye, fferie

      Pronunciation

      [edit]
      • IPA(key): /ˈfɛːriː(ə)/

      Noun

      [edit]

      ferie (plural feries)

      1. A weekday; a day of the working week.
      2. A feria; a day that isn't a festival.
      Related terms
      [edit]
      • ferial
      Descendants
      [edit]
      • English: ferie (obsolete)
      References
      [edit]
      • “fēri(e, n.(1).”, in MED Online, Ann Arbor, Mich.: University of Michigan, 2007.

      Polish

      [edit]
      Polish Wikipedia has an article on:
      ferie
      Wikipedia pl

      Etymology

      [edit]

      Learned borrowing from Latin fēriae.

      Pronunciation

      [edit]
      • IPA(key): /ˈfɛ.rjɛ/
      • Audio:(file)
      • Rhymes: -ɛrjɛ
      • Syllabification: fe‧rie

      Noun

      [edit]

      ferie nvir pl

      1. winter vacation
      2. (education) winter school break

      Declension

      [edit]
      Declension of ferie
      plural
      nominative ferie
      genitive ferii/feryj (archaic)
      dative feriom
      accusative ferie
      instrumental feriami
      locative feriach
      vocative ferie

      Further reading

      • ferie in Polish dictionaries at PWN
